title: Non Overlapping Intervals
description: Given a list of `[start, end]` intervals, return the minimum number of intervals you must remove so that the remaining ones do not overlap. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint, such as `[1,2]` and `[2,4]`, do **not** overlap.
hints: Removing the fewest intervals is the same as keeping the most intervals that do not overlap.
Among overlapping intervals, which one leaves the most room for later ones: the one that ends earliest or latest?
Sort by end. Keep an interval if its start >= the last kept end; otherwise count a removal.

solution.explanation: This is interval scheduling: maximize the number of kept intervals. Sort by end time, then greedily keep each interval whose start is at or after the end of the last kept one; an interval that starts earlier overlaps and is counted as removed. Picking the earliest-ending interval always leaves the most room for the rest. Sorting costs O(n log n) and the sweep is O(n).
